_: English glossary for the book's 'Words of the day' box. Keys are the same code terms used in the Turkish data (explain.terms).
print(): Prints what is inside the parentheses. Values separated by commas get a space between them.
*: Multiplication; also repeats text or a list ("*" * 3 → "***").
=: Assignment: puts the value on the right into the name on the left. (Use == to compare.)
+: Addition; joins text and lists end to end.
int(): Turns a value into a whole number, e.g. the text "42" into the number 42.
//: Floor division: the whole part of the result (7 // 2 → 3).
%: Modulo: the remainder of a division (7 % 2 → 1).
+=: Adds to the variable's own value: x += 1 → x = x + 1.
-=: Subtracts from the variable's value: x -= 1 → x = x - 1.
/: Division; the result is always a decimal number.
*=: Multiplies the variable: x *= 2 → x = x * 2.
[ ]: Picks an item with square brackets: by position (starting at 0) or by dictionary key.
-: Subtraction, or the minus sign in front of a number.
f\"...{}\": Text starting with f; the values of the variables inside {} are placed into the text.
[a:b]: Slicing: takes the part from a up to b (b not included).
.append(): Adds a new item to the end of the list.
.remove(): Removes the given item from a list (or set).
sum(): Adds up the numbers in a list.
len(): Gives the number of items (the length) of a text, list or dictionary.
sorted(): Gives a new sorted list; the original list doesn't change.
list(): Makes a list from a value, or an empty list.
tuple(): Makes a tuple (a list that can't be changed) from a value.
set(): Makes a set (a collection without duplicates) from a value.
.add(): Adds a new item to the set.
.discard(): Removes an item from the set; no error if it isn't there.
&: Set intersection: items that are in both sets.
|: Set union: everything from both sets.
if: If the condition is true, the indented lines below it run.
else: Runs if none of the conditions above were true.
.get(): Gets the value of a key from a dictionary; if the key is missing it gives a default instead of an error.
elif: If the previous conditions were false, this condition is checked ("else if").
and: "and": True if both conditions are true.
or: "or": True if at least one condition is true.
in: Is it inside? (in a list, text or dictionary)
is not: Is it a different object? (x is not None: is x not empty?)
input(): Asks the user to type a line and gives it back as text (str).
while: Repeats the lines below it as long as the condition is true.
for: Repeats the lines below it for every item in a list (or range).
range(): Makes a sequence of numbers: range(5) → 0, 1, 2, 3, 4. The last number is not included.
enumerate(): While going through a list, also gives each item's position: (0, first), (1, second)...
continue: Skips the rest of this round of the loop and moves to the next one.
def: Defines a new function; the inside doesn't run until it's called.
return: Sends a value back from a function and ends the function.
import: Adds a module (a library of ready-made code) to the program.
random: Functions for random numbers and choices.
.randint(): Picks a random whole number between two numbers (both included).
.choice(): Picks a random item from a list.
[... for ... in ...]: List comprehension: [expression for x in list if condition] builds a new list in one line.
lambda: A tiny one-line function without a name.
map(): Applies a function to every item of a list.
filter(): Keeps only the items of a list that pass a condition.
date: Represents a date (year, month, day) (from the datetime module).
date(): Represents a date (year, month, day) (from the datetime module).
.strftime(): Turns a date into text in the format you want, e.g. "%d.%m.%Y".
timedelta: Represents a length of time (days, hours...) between two dates.
timedelta(): Represents a length of time (days, hours...) between two dates.
.weekday(): Gives the day of the week as a number (0 = Monday).
try: Tries code that might fail; if an error happens, the except block runs.
except: Runs if an error happens inside try; the program doesn't crash.
None: A special value that means "nothing / empty".
ValueError(): The kind of error raised when a value isn't suitable.
re: Regular expressions: searching for patterns in text.
.findall(): Gives a list of every part of the text that matches the pattern (re).
.search(): Finds the first place in the text that matches the pattern (re).
.sub(): Replaces the parts that match the pattern with something else (re).
.fullmatch(): Checks whether the whole text matches the pattern (re).
.group(): Gives the text of the match (or of a group in parentheses).
with: Opens resources like files and closes them automatically when the block ends.
open(): Opens a file for reading or writing. "r" read, "w" write, "a" append.
.read(): Reads the whole file as text.
json: Writing and reading data in JSON format.
.dump(): Writes the data to a file as JSON.
.load(): Reads the JSON in a file and turns it into Python data.
os: Operating system tools (does a file exist?, folders...).
.exists(): Does the given file or folder exist? (True/False)
.split(): Splits text into pieces and makes a list (by default at spaces).
.strip(): Removes spaces at the start and end of the text.
A if ... else B: A one-line condition: A if condition else B.
.items(): Gives the (key, value) pairs of a dictionary.
.join(): Joins the texts in a list with the text in between: ", ".join(list)
class: Defines a new class (a blueprint for objects).
__init__(): The setup method that runs automatically when a new object is created from a class.
self: Inside a class it means "this object itself".
super(): Gives access to the methods of the parent class (the class it inherits from).
bs4: A library for reading HTML pages (BeautifulSoup).
BeautifulSoup: Reads an HTML page and lets you search inside it (bs4).
BeautifulSoup(): Reads an HTML page and lets you search inside it (bs4).
.find_all(): Finds every tag of the given kind in the HTML (bs4).
.copy(): Makes a copy of a list/dictionary.
.startswith(): Does the text start with the given text? (True/False)
.endswith(): Does the text end with the given text? (True/False)
.median(): Finds the median (the middle value when sorted).
numpy: A library for fast calculations with arrays of numbers.
.array(): Creates a NumPy array (a fast list of numbers).
pandas: A library for working with table (row-column) data.
.DataFrame(): Creates a pandas table (rows and columns).
.tolist(): Turns an array into a normal Python list.
.sort_values(): Sorts the table by a column.
.read_csv(): Reads CSV data into a pandas table.
.StringIO(): Lets you use a piece of text as if it were a file.
.sum(): Adds up the values (of a column or group).
.groupby(): Groups the table by a column.
.idxmax(): Gives the row where the largest value is.
all(): Gives True if all items are true.
.update(): Adds new key-value pairs to a dictionary or changes existing ones.
isinstance(): Asks whether a value is of a certain type (True/False).
.loads(): Turns JSON text into Python data (dictionary, list).
.isdigit(): Is the text made only of digits? (True/False)
.replace(): Replaces a part of the text with something else.
